info.name: Inventory & Orders API
info.description:
# Inventory & Orders API

Laravel REST API for products, customers and orders.

## Before you start

1. Import `Local-Environment.postman_environment.json` and select it.
2. Seed the database: `php artisan migrate:fresh --seed`
3. Start the app: `php artisan serve`
4. Check `product_id_1/2/3` and `low_stock_product_id` point at real ids (see the README).

## Authentication

Every endpoint except `POST /api/auth/token` requires a Sanctum bearer token.

Run **00 - Authentication > Issue token** first. Its test script saves the token into
the `auth_token` environment variable, which every other request reads automatically.

## Recommended run order

1. `00 - Authentication` > Issue token
2. `01 - Create order` (top to bottom - later requests reuse saved variables)
3. `02 - Create order (expected failures)`
4. `03 - Customer order history`
5. `04 - Low stock products`
6. `00 - Authentication` > Revoke the current token (last)

## Requests that are meant to fail

Anything named `FAILS:` is expected to return a 4xx status. Its tests assert that
failure, so a green result means the API correctly rejected bad input.

## Security note

This collection contains no real credentials. The values in the environment file are
local development placeholders that match the database seeder.

item.name: Server ignores client-supplied prices and totals

exec: pm.test("Unit price came from the product catalogue", () => {

request.description:
SECURITY CHECK. The body deliberately contains fake prices, tax rates and totals. 

The order is still created (201), but every monetary figure is recalculated from the products table. If this request ever returned a grand_total of 0.01, the API would be critically broken.

item.name: 02 - Create order (expected failures)
item.description: Every request in this folder is EXPECTED TO FAIL. They prove validation and stock protection work.

exec: pm.test("Response names the product and the shortfall", () => {

request.description:
EXPECTED TO FAIL (409 Conflict).

Orders far more than the available stock of a deliberately low-stock product. 409 rather than 422: the payload is well formed, but the current state of the world cannot satisfy it.

Nothing is written - no order, and no customer row.
EXPECTED TO FAIL (422). The name is too short and the email is malformed.
EXPECTED TO FAIL (422). Product 999999999 does not exist.
EXPECTED TO FAIL (422). Quantity must be a positive integer, so 0 is rejected. Negative and fractional quantities are rejected the same way.
EXPECTED TO FAIL (422). An order must contain at least one line item.

item.name: FAILS: duplicate product in one order

request.description:
EXPECTED TO FAIL (422).

Documented behaviour: the same product may not appear twice in one order. The client should combine the lines into a single item with the total quantity. The order_items table enforces the same rule with a unique(order_id, product_id) constraint.

exec: pm.test("The response reports the default threshold was applied", () => {
pm.test("Every product returned is at or below the threshold", () => {
pm.test("Results are ordered lowest stock first", () => {

request.description:
No threshold parameter, so the configured default is used (INVENTORY_LOW_STOCK_THRESHOLD, default 10).

The comparison is <=, so a product sitting exactly on the threshold IS included.

exec: pm.test("No product exceeds the requested threshold", () => {

request.description: Overrides the default with threshold=5.
EXPECTED TO FAIL (422). Stock cannot be negative, so a negative threshold is a client bug.

item.name: FAILS: threshold above the allowed maximum

request.description:
EXPECTED TO FAIL (422).

The threshold is capped (INVENTORY_LOW_STOCK_MAX_THRESHOLD, default 1000) so this endpoint cannot be used to dump the entire catalogue in one request.

item.name: 05 - Clean up (run last)
item.description: Revokes the bearer token. Deliberately the final folder so the collection can be run straight through.

item.name: Revoke the current token

request.description:
Revokes the token used to make this request.

Run this LAST: afterwards {{auth_token}} is no longer valid and you must issue a new one.

item.description:
Revokes the token used to make this request.

This lives in its own folder so a top-to-bottom run reaches it LAST. Running it earlier would invalidate {{auth_token}} and every subsequent request would return 401.

After this runs, issue a new token before using the collection again.
